title: Polynomial-time clean implementation
statement: For every finite-state binary Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $C,e$, there are a finite-state binary Turing machine $W$ with at least one work tape, entry and exit states of $W$, and natural numbers $a,d$, such that for every Boolean input word $x$ and argument word $u$, some time $t$ satisfies $0<t\le a(|u|+1)^d$. Starting from the configuration on input $x$ with $W$ in its entry state and with $u$ on the first work tape and all other work tapes blank, the run has not reached the exit state at any intermediate time $j$ with $0<j<t$, and at time $t$ it is exactly the configuration with $W$ in its exit state and the first tape holding the producer-step result on $u$, all other work tapes blank, and the same input-head position and empty output.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-state binary machine W with at least one work tape exists
Entry and exit states of W exist
Natural numbers a and d exist
There exists t with 0 < t ≤ a(|u|+1)^d
No intermediate time j with 0 < j < t has state equal to the exit state
replaced: For every source machine and parameters $C$ and $e$, there are a machine, entry and exit controls, and constants such that each producer step has a clean reusable native call: a strictly positive first exit within a polynomial of the argument length, returning exactly the stepped state word with all scratch restored. The variable number of such calls is not yet assembled here.
